0.long_answer: The cancer described is a rare and aggressive T-cell lymphoma that is not associated with HTLV-1 infection. Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma is usually linked to HTLV-1, so when a patient presents with lymphadenopathy (enlarged lymph nodes) and hepatosplenomegaly (enlargement of the liver and spleen) but tests negative for HTLV-1, the diagnosis is more consistent with a T-cell lymphoma that does not harbor this virus. In this context, the condition best fitting this description is Peripheral T-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (PTCL-NOS). This type of lymphoma is a heterogeneous group of aggressive T-cell neoplasms that present with systemic involvement and generally have a worse prognosis than many B-cell lymphomas.
0.short_answer: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (PTCL-NOS)
